title: Active rooks in rook endings

D0.outcome: Explains that a rook belongs behind a passed pawn (its own or the enemy's) and that an active rook is often worth more than a pawn.

D1.outcome: Placing the rook correctly in simple rook-and-pawn positions (behind the passer, on the seventh, cutting the king off).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled rook endings, chooses between passive defence and active counterplay, and between winning a pawn and activity.

D3.outcome: Predicts which side's rook is tied, and knows when the passive rook is the only draw.

misconceptions: Never defend passively in a rook ending.
An extra pawn wins rook endings.
conditions: Rook and pawn or minor-piece endings with pawns on both wings.
Placing a rook behind the opponent's passed pawn freezes the opposing rook.
contrasts: Passive defence is sometimes the only draw.
An extra pawn wins rook endings.
A king move that changes nothing in the rook ending.
